Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States Mixed Fed on hold / growth split
🇪🇺 European Union Bullish ECB on hold / relative winner
🇨🇳 China Mixed easing bias / weak demand
🇯🇵 Japan Bullish BOJ normalising / strong yen
🇵🇱 Poland Bullish easing pause / growth re-accelerating
🔬 US–Asia Semis — SOXX / ASML / TSMC Bullish
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Guidance and tariffs decide the tape
🔍 Underowned Themes — Attention and Exposure Gaps
Quality software after the AI purge
Oilfield services for the Venezuela reopening
Coinbase's loss confirms the crypto earnings recession
Bonds bid, dollar flat, money leaving US equities
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
$ABNB — travel guidance beats the consumer gloom Bullish
Silver / SLV — catching the flash crash
Micron & SanDisk / MU, SNDK — memory mania
Strategy / MSTR — a bitcoin proxy at a 73% drawdown
body: Friday, February 13 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information cutoff: 2026-02-13 00:00 UTC. Market figures use completed observations before this date.

Macro Stance: The data now pull in opposite directions: January payrolls rose 130,000 and unemployment fell to 4.3% CNBC [Feb 11], but January home sales posted their biggest monthly decline in nearly four years WSJ [Feb 12]. Equities broke as the tech rout deepened on AI angst Reuters [Feb 12]; the S&P 500 fell 1.57% to 6,832.76 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Mixed: jobs argue against cuts, housing and the tape against complacency.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.47% and the 10Y at 4.09%, a 10Y−2Y spread of +62 bps — moderately steep, approaching the long-run average; over 20 observations the move is a bull flattening (2Y −4 bps, 10Y −6 bps, spread −2 bps), and over five observations the 10Y fell 12 bps while the 2Y was unchanged (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-12). VIX jumped 3.17 points to 20.82 while DXY held at 96.93 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

New / Most Important: The January CPI report is due out Friday morning CNBC [Feb 12], and Fed Governor Miran argues policy is tighter than thought and inflation is not a problem Reuters [Feb 12] — the dovish case a soft print would validate. The Senate also blocked Homeland Security funding, raising the likelihood of a shutdown Reuters [Feb 12].

Playbook ✓: Rotate from cyclicals to quality defensives into CPI: own staples retail and regulated utilities, trim industrials, and hold duration while the 10Y trends lower at 4.09% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-12). Hedge equity beta with VIX call spreads while VIX sits above 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Re-risk into cyclicals only if core CPI is soft and the S&P 500 reclaims its 20-session reference of 6,926.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-14).

Macro Stance: The ECB is set to extend its longest interest-rate pause since the below-zero era Reuters [Feb 12], and Makhlouf says the next move could be a cut or a hike Bloomberg [Feb 12] — policy is anchored and two-sided. Europe remains the relative winner: the STOXX 600 is up 0.64% over 20 sessions while the S&P 500 is down 1.35% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). We stay bullish on European equities, but selectively.

Activity & Inflation: EUR/USD closed at 1.1876, up 1.97% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12), a disinflationary headwind for exporters; the DAX is down 1.97% over 20 sessions while the CAC 40 is up 0.33% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Siemens shares jumped on a lifted outlook WSJ [Feb 12] — evidence that industrial demand is improving despite the stronger euro.

New / Most Important: European shares retreated from record highs as financials and industrials tumbled Reuters [Feb 12]; the STOXX 600 slipped 0.49% to 618.52 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). The AI-disruption trade is now hitting European financials as well as software, removing one of the rally's two sector pillars.

Playbook ✓: Keep the STOXX 600 overweight against US equities but rotate within it: add automation winners on results such as Siemens WSJ [Feb 12], hold energy, and cut wealth managers and asset-light financials exposed to AI disruption. Change the call if the euro's 20-session gain extends while the ECB stays on hold — that combination tightens conditions for exporters.

Macro Stance: The domestic economy remains soft — consumer prices rose just 0.2% in January China Daily [Feb 11] — while diplomacy improves: Reuters reports Trump has paused China tech bans ahead of a Xi summit Reuters [Feb 12], the most constructive US–China signal in months. We stay Mixed: better geopolitics and a strong yuan, but no domestic demand recovery yet.

PMIs & Activity: The latest official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3 in January Reuters [Jan 30], back below 50, and the feed carries no fresh February activity data. With mainland markets about to close for the holiday, the next official PMI is the confirmation point; a reading back above 50 would be needed to upgrade the domestic view, and Spring Festival spending is the interim consumption test.

Credit Impulse: The latest full-year print shows 2025 new bank loans at a seven-year low, with Reuters noting that policy support is needed Reuters [Jan 15]. The feed still carries no January credit release, so the impulse remains unconfirmed; January is seasonally the largest lending month. A rise in household medium- and long-term loans would be the signal that property demand is reviving — corporate bill financing would not.

Property: New-home prices extended their decline as weak demand hounds the sector Reuters [Feb 12], and state firms are buying foreclosed properties to slow the downturn Reuters [Feb 12] — the state is now absorbing inventory directly. That builds a floor under prices rather than a recovery; avoid developers and wait for price declines to narrow before adding property-linked exposure.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Trade remains the strong leg: China's annual trade surplus hit a record $1.2 trillion even as exports to the US fell 20% CNBC [Jan 13]. Exporters have diversified away from the US, which is why the surplus keeps widening despite tariffs. What is missing is a direct transfer to households, which is why CPI stays close to zero.

Markets & Flows: The Shanghai Composite closed at 4,134.02, up 0.52% over 20 sessions, while the Hang Seng fell 0.86% to 27,032.54; ASHR is at 33.82, but KWEB fell 3.84% to 32.79 and is down 10.95% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). USD/CNY is 6.9125, down 0.87% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12), with the yuan at its strongest since 2023 Bloomberg.com [Feb 09]. Mainland markets close February 16–23 for the Lunar New Year investingLive [Feb 12], so the next reaction will run through Hong Kong.

New / Most Important: The Xi-summit track is the new swing factor: pausing tech bans Reuters [Feb 12] reduces the immediate risk of new US restrictions. Offshore internet did not benefit — KWEB's 3.84% drop tracked the US tech selloff (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) — so the opportunity sits in names that fell with US tech despite better bilateral news.

Playbook ✓: Keep onshore exposure via ASHR, add selectively to Hong Kong tech before the holiday closure, and keep developers underweight. Upgrade to Bullish on a confirmed summit plus a January credit beat. ⚠ Divergence: a record trade surplus CNBC [Jan 13] and a yuan at its strongest since 2023 Bloomberg.com [Feb 09] sit against new-home prices that are still falling Reuters [Feb 12] — external strength is not reaching households.

Macro Stance: BOJ hawk Tamura signalled a rate-hike chance 'this spring' Reuters [Feb 12], reinforcing the normalisation path under Takaichi's new mandate. SoftBank's fourth straight quarterly profit on its OpenAI gain Reuters [Feb 12] keeps Tokyo's AI exposure earning. We stay Bullish: reflation plus rate normalisation favours banks and domestic demand.

Activity & Currency: The Nikkei 225 closed flat at 57,639.84, down 0.02% in the session but up 6.07% over 20 sessions, a Tokyo close that preceded the Wall Street selloff (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). USD/JPY fell 0.79% to 153.27 and is down 3.24% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12), and Reuters notes the yen is set for a strong weekly finish Reuters [Feb 12].

Playbook ✓: Own banks and domestic-demand names, trim exporters and keep yen hedges light. Add on a confirmed spring hike signal Reuters [Feb 12]. Cut if USD/JPY rebounds toward its 20-session reference of 158.4020 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-15), which would signal carry rebuilding and a loss of policy credibility.

Macro Stance: The RBA conceded that low unemployment fuelled inflation AFR [Feb 12], cementing a hawkish bias after the February hike, and the AFR sees the Australian dollar heading to the 'mid-70s' in US cents as the RBA raises rates AFR [Feb 12]. A hawkish central bank and a strong currency squeeze the domestic consumer — Mixed.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD rose 0.71% to 0.7125 and is up 6.62% over 20 sessions; the ASX 200 gained 0.32% to 9,043.50 and is up 2.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Morningstar's chart of the week shows a soft earnings-growth outlook for Australian banks Morningstar Australia [Feb 12], so the bank-led rally rests on capital returns rather than growth.

Playbook ✓: Stay long AUD/USD on rate differentials, take profits in the major banks into strength, and avoid rate-sensitive retailers. Change the call if the next quarterly CPI undershoots or unemployment rises — given the RBA's admission on the labour market AFR [Feb 12], either would price the second hike out quickly.

Monetary & Activity: GDP growth accelerated to 4% (Bankier: 'the Polish economy jumps to a higher level') Bankier.pl [Feb 12], and Polish bond yields fell below 5%, the lowest in two years Bankier.pl [Feb 12] — strong growth with falling yields, an equity-friendly mix. Fitch's warning that Poland risks a downgrade if debt is not stabilised Reuters [Feb 10] remains the main macro risk.

FX & Markets: USD/PLN closed at 3.5480, down 1.85% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN at 4.2115 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). EPOL fell 1.25% to 37.91 but is up 5.22% over 20 sessions, and the WIG20TR ETF is up 3.36% at 67.94; Orlen (PKN) is up 10.7% over 20 sessions at 110.48 and Pekao 10.16% at 229.80 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

Companies: The CJEU's WIBOR ruling went the banks' way — Rzeczpospolita: 'WIBOR will not be a second Swiss franc' Rzeczpospolita [Feb 12] — and Money.pl notes it did not shake bank shares Money.pl [Feb 12]; PKO BP closed at 92.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). CD Projekt targets 5 bn zł of profit over 2026-2029 (Bankier) Bankier.pl [Feb 12]; the stock rose 1.16% to 244.00 but is down 11.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

Security & New Development: EU ambassadors approved a €44bn loan for Poland under the SAFE defence programme polskieradio.pl [Feb 10], funding the domestic arms build-up and the defence supply chain. With the WIBOR overhang lifted, bank shares now trade on rates and credit growth rather than legal risk.

Playbook ✓: Upgrade Polish banks from neutral to overweight after the WIBOR relief; keep Orlen and PGE as core holdings and leave the zloty unhedged. Cut if Fitch moves to a negative outlook or bond yields climb back above 5% Bankier.pl [Feb 12]. ⚠ Divergence: 4% growth Bankier.pl [Feb 12] and two-year-low yields coexist with Fitch's debt warning Reuters [Feb 10] — the market is pricing the cycle, not the fiscal trajectory.

Narrative: The AI-disruption trade has turned on tech itself. XLK fell 2.63% in the prior session and is down 3.79% over 20 sessions, with Apple down 5.0% to 261.73 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). MarketWatch says Cisco's stock fell hard and took the tech sector with it MarketWatch [Feb 12] — hardware is no longer immune when guidance disappoints.

Reported: Cisco's post-earnings drop MarketWatch [Feb 12] set the tone: a beat with a mediocre outlook is now a sell signal. Microsoft slipped 0.63% to 401.84 and is down 12.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

EPS Upside Watch: Infrastructure software with usage-based pricing: AWS CEO Garman says software AI fears are 'overblown' CNBC [Feb 12], and Oracle is up 14.65% over five sessions despite a 19.18% 20-session drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) — buyers are returning to the infrastructure layer first.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Apple, the perceived AI-safe haven, fell 5.0% in a day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) — there is no defensive corner left in megacap tech. Bearish until the sector stops falling on good news.

Narrative: Communication services lost its defensive status: XLC fell 1.8% in the prior session, with Disney down 5.31%, Netflix 4.72% and Meta 2.82% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Ad-funded platforms are being repriced for tariff-hit advertisers and AI-search competition.

Reported: Pinterest shares tanked as its CEO blamed tariffs for a revenue miss and weak outlook CNBC [Feb 12], while Roku forecast upbeat annual revenue on platform strength and its shares jumped Reuters [Feb 12]. Connected-TV is winning ad share; discovery and social platforms are losing it.

EPS Upside Watch: Connected-TV platforms where ad budgets are migrating Reuters [Feb 12]; Alphabet, down only 0.63% on the day at 309.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12), remains the cheapest scaled ad franchise after its 20-session drawdown.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Netflix is down 14.33% over 20 sessions at 75.86 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) — subscription streaming, the old 'defensive growth' trade, now trades like software. Bearish: avoid ad-dependent mid-caps until tariff effects on ad budgets fade.

Narrative: Financials are the AI-disruption trade's second casualty. XLF fell 1.99% in the prior session and is down 4.54% over 20 sessions; Goldman Sachs dropped 4.24%, JPMorgan 2.63% and Bank of America 2.47% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Barron's says AI fears hit Charles Schwab and other financial stocks Barron's [Feb 12].

Reported: No major US bank reported in the window; the newsflow is about valuation and business-model risk. In Europe, Schroders popped 28% on a Nuveen takeover set to create an asset-management giant CNBC [Feb 12] — consolidation is the industry's answer to fee pressure.

EPS Upside Watch: Exchanges and trading-heavy banks benefit from volatility, with VIX at 20.82 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12), and Barron's makes the case for buying the AI-hit names now Barron's [Feb 12].

⚡ Breaking Convention: The takeover premium for Schroders CNBC [Feb 12] shows strategic buyers value the asset-management franchises public markets are selling on AI fears — a floor under the sector. Bearish near term, but build a watch-list of AI-hit brokers for the rebound.

Narrative: Energy's rally met the fundamentals: oil fell 3% as the IEA reduced its demand forecast CNBC [Feb 12]. Brent closed at 67.52, down 2.71%, and WTI at 62.84, down 2.77%; XLE fell 1.82% but is still up 12.32% over 20 sessions and Exxon 15.15% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).
Reported: No major US producer reported in the window; the demand outlook did the talking, and the IEA cut CNBC [Feb 12] removes the fundamental support for a further leg higher in crude.

EPS Upside Watch: Integrateds with Venezuelan optionality: US-led oil sales from Venezuela are expected to bring in $5 billion in months Reuters [Feb 12], supporting Chevron's volume story; CVX is up 9.06% over 20 sessions at 182.40 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

⚡ Breaking Convention: XLE is up double digits over 20 sessions while Brent is up only 1.5% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) — energy equities are trading as a rotation vehicle, not an oil call. Mixed: hold integrateds, hedge with Brent puts.

Narrative: Industrials remain the cyclical leadership despite the selloff: XLI fell 1.2% in the prior session but is up 5.16% over 20 sessions, and Caterpillar is up 18.71% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Siemens shares jumped on a lifted outlook WSJ [Feb 12], a European confirmation of the automation upturn.

Reported: Machine-vision maker Cognex soared as manufacturing improves Barron's [Feb 12]. Trucking and logistics stocks dropped on the release of an AI freight-scaling tool CNBC [Feb 12] — the AI-disruption trade has reached transport brokers.

EPS Upside Watch: Factory-automation suppliers — Siemens, Cognex, Rockwell — where improving manufacturing orders flow straight into high-margin product revenue Barron's [Feb 12]. Boeing rose 1.31% to 239.35 on the down day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12), a sign aerospace backlogs are being treated as visible, tariff-light earnings.

⚡ Breaking Convention: AI is a negative for asset-light freight intermediaries CNBC [Feb 12] and a positive for physical automation: within industrials, own the hardware and avoid the brokers. Bullish.

Narrative: Consumer discretionary is caught between weak housing and a cautious consumer: XLY fell 1.38% and is down 5.01% over 20 sessions, Amazon 15.66% at 199.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). The value end is winning — McDonald's sales topped forecasts as value and promotions boosted US results for a third straight quarter Yahoo Finance [Feb 12].

Reported: Airbnb rose on a revenue beat and rosy guidance CNBC [Feb 12], while Restaurant Brands fell despite a beat and strong international growth CNBC [Feb 12]. Tesla fell 2.62% to 417.07 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

EPS Upside Watch: Travel platforms with pricing power, led by Airbnb's guidance CNBC [Feb 12], and value restaurants Yahoo Finance [Feb 12]: they monetise the affluent and the budget ends of the K-shaped consumer respectively.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Home Depot is up 3.8% over 20 sessions at 390.22 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) even as home sales plunged — owners locked into old mortgages renovate instead of moving. Bearish on the sector, selective on travel and home improvement.
Narrative: Staples were the haven in the selloff: XLP rose 0.92% and is up 8.49% over 20 sessions, with Walmart up 3.78% to 133.64 and Costco 2.12% to 998.86 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

Reported: Unilever was downbeat on 2026 sales growth amid a US and European slowdown Reuters [Feb 12], and ice-cream maker Magnum's shares slumped as debut results underwhelmed Reuters [Feb 12] — brand owners are not sharing the retailers' strength.

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart and Costco: Walmart is up 11.33% over 20 sessions and Costco 5.03% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12), with earnings leverage coming from grocery scale, membership income and e-commerce share gains rather than price. Both are the natural destination for money leaving megacap tech while keeping quality.
⚡ Breaking Convention: The staples rally is a retailer rally — Unilever's caution Reuters [Feb 12] shows branded volume is still weak. Bullish on staples retail, underweight branded packaged goods.

Narrative: Health care held up as a defensive: XLV slipped 0.16%, while Lilly rose 2.27% to 1,038.27 and UnitedHealth 1.96% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Obesity drugs remain the growth engine; managed care remains the margin problem.
Reported: ICON shares plunged 50% after a revenue-overstatement disclosure Yahoo Finance [Feb 12] — a reminder that accounting risk at service providers can wipe out a defensive position overnight.
EPS Upside Watch: Lilly: a 2.27% gain on a risk-off day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) shows investors using it as a growth defensive, with obesity volumes the main growth driver.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The administration is being urged to use a federal law to authorize generic GLP-1 drugs STAT [Feb 12] — obesity pricing power is now a policy target. Mixed: own pharma growth, but size obesity exposure for pricing risk.

Narrative: Precious metals broke: gold fell 2.94% to 4,948.40 and silver 9.8% to 75.55, with Freeport down 5.22% and Newmont 5.2% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Reuters says gold cascaded down as strong US jobs data and stop-selling weighed Reuters [Feb 12].
Reported: No major US materials company reported in the window; the verdict came from the tape, where XLB fell 1.47% but remains up 8.37% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

EPS Upside Watch: Copper supply is tightening — global smelting activity hit a decade low Mining.com [Feb 12] — which supports miners' realised prices even after copper fell 2.99% to 5.77 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Gold is still up 6.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12): the flash crash flushed leverage, not the thesis. Mixed — buy miners once positioning cleans up, avoid leveraged silver.

Narrative: Falling yields are offsetting AI fears in real estate: XLRE rose 0.16% while the S&P 500 fell and is up 3.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12), with the 10Y down to 4.09% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-12). Mortgage rates dipped back down to near three-year lows Yahoo Finance [Feb 12].

Reported: Reporting was light; the share reactions came from the AI trade instead — office real estate stocks tumbled as AI-disruption casualties grew by the day CNBC [Feb 12]. The sector held up overall because falling yields outweighed the office drag.
EPS Upside Watch: Residential and net-lease REITs: lower mortgage rates Yahoo Finance [Feb 12] and a 10Y at 4.09% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-12) cut funding costs and support asset values.
⚡ Breaking Convention: Office landlords are now priced as AI losers — fewer white-collar workers means less space CNBC [Feb 12]. Bullish on rate-sensitive residential and net-lease, avoid office.

Narrative: Utilities were the best-performing defensive: XLU rose 1.48% and is up 4.82% over 20 sessions, with NextEra up 12.14% and Vistra 14.0% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Falling yields plus data-centre capex make the sector a growth-defensive hybrid, but Constellation is still down 16.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) — the market prefers regulated rate base to merchant nuclear.
Reported: Duke claims the largest spending plan of any regulated US utility at $103B Utility Dive [Feb 12] — rate-base growth is the earnings engine.

EPS Upside Watch: Regulated utilities with large capex plans Utility Dive [Feb 12] compound earnings as long as regulators allow recovery; those with large-load tariffs that bill data centres directly carry the least risk.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Reuters warns affordability concerns loom as utilities spend big on data-centre demand Reuters [Feb 12] — the bigger the capex plan, the bigger the regulatory risk. Bullish on regulated names with large-load tariffs, cautious on those without.

Narrative: European autos remain the weakest link in Europe: Mercedes' 2025 earnings more than halved on tariff costs and China woes Automotive News [Feb 12], and MBG is down 3.76% over 20 sessions at 57.11 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

Reported: The Mercedes result Automotive News [Feb 12] confirms tariffs and China are structural margin drags, not one-offs. The EXV5 autos tracker still rose 0.83% on the day to 46.22, while BMW fell 1.95% to 87.72 and VOW3 1.21% to 102.30 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) — the German premium names carry the most China risk.

EPS Upside Watch: Renault, up 2.19%, and Stellantis, up 3.67% at 7.90 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12), are rebounding from depressed levels — short-covering rather than upgrades, so treat rallies as exits.
⚡ Breaking Convention: China softened its stance on EV makers negotiating with the EU individually Reuters [Feb 12] — the door to Chinese price competition in Europe is opening further. Bearish.

Narrative: Semis sold off with tech — SOXX fell 2.42% — but remain up 6.25% over five sessions and 5.91% over 20, with Micron up 0.88% to 413.97 against the tape (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). The memory squeeze still drives the group.
Reported: Applied Materials' stock jumped after earnings, and its CEO made a bold prediction for the chip sector MarketWatch [Feb 12] — confirmation that equipment demand is accelerating.

EPS Upside Watch: Memory and equipment: Samsung began commercial shipments of HBM4 to a customer Bloomberg.com [Feb 12], signalling the next AI-memory cycle is under way — supportive for equipment orders, though it adds competition for Micron.

⚡ Breaking Convention: US lawmakers demand a ban on chipmaking-tool sales to China, targeting ASML's lithography exports Tom's Hardware [Feb 12]; ASML fell 2.0% to 1,406.87 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Bullish on the group, but prefer memory and US equipment over ASML until the policy risk clears.

Rewarded: Raised outlooks were bought: Applied Materials jumped after earnings MarketWatch [Feb 12], Airbnb rose on rosy guidance CNBC [Feb 12], Siemens on a lifted outlook WSJ [Feb 12], and Cognex on improving manufacturing Barron's [Feb 12].

Punished: Weak outlooks were sold hard: Pinterest tanked as its CEO blamed tariffs CNBC [Feb 12], Adyen hit a two-year low after a revenue miss and a flat adjusted-earnings forecast WSJ [Feb 12], and ICON lost 50% on a revenue-overstatement disclosure Yahoo Finance [Feb 12]. Coinbase posted a $667 million loss as revenue tumbled 20% Bloomberg.com [Feb 12].

Pattern: The market pays for forward visibility in capex-linked hardware, automation and travel, and punishes ad-dependent and payments platforms where tariffs or AI threaten pricing. A beat with a cautious outlook — Cisco MarketWatch [Feb 12], Restaurant Brands CNBC [Feb 12] — is treated as a miss. Two weeks into the season, the asymmetry has widened: raised guidance is rewarded, while outlooks that cite tariffs or AI competition are punished hard. That is the signature of a market long quality and short anything with a margin question.

Attention into EPS: Nvidia is the next big test — the Motley Fool asks whether to buy the stock before Feb. 25 The Motley Fool [Feb 08] — after Applied Materials' bullish chip-sector call MarketWatch [Feb 12]. Into Friday's CPI, management commentary on tariffs will matter more than reported EPS.

Playbook: Buy beat-and-raise in semis equipment, automation and travel on the first pullback; avoid ad-funded platforms and payments names that cite tariffs or AI pressure. Change the call if a guidance-cut name rallies on the day — the first sign of capitulation in the punished cohort.

Attention Gap: The AI-disruption narrative has spread to financials, trucking and office property, yet the operator view is moving the other way: AWS CEO Garman calls software AI fears 'overblown' CNBC [Feb 12]. Microsoft is down 12.53% over 20 sessions at 401.84 and Palantir 27.62% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) — profitable platforms are priced like the disrupted.

Exposure & Risk: Build in large, profitable platforms (Microsoft, Salesforce) or IGV in tranches; avoid small-cap SaaS. Risks: each new AI release triggers another leg lower, and the selloff now reaches lenders and brokers, as Barron's notes for Schwab Barron's [Feb 12]. Add only on days when bad news fails to make new lows.

Attention Gap: US-led oil sales from Venezuela are expected to bring in $5 billion in months Reuters [Feb 12], yet investor focus stays on the majors' caution rather than the service and supply contracts that must come first when production is rebuilt. Rebuilding degraded fields is service-intensive work — workovers, artificial lift, pipe and power — which shows up in service revenue well before it shows up in barrels.

Exposure & Risk: Express via SLB, Halliburton, Baker Hughes or OIH, with Chevron as the integrated proxy — CVX is up 9.06% over 20 sessions at 182.40 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). Risks: the IEA's demand cut CNBC [Feb 12] caps upstream budgets, and political reversal in Caracas or Washington.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 66,221.84, down 1.15% on the day and 26.01% over 20 sessions; ether closed at 1,946.94, down 34.07%, and solana at 78.35, down 38.48% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). COIN fell 7.9% to 141.09 before its results and is down 44.86% over 20 sessions; MSTR is down 31.41% and IBIT 33.17% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

New / Most Important: Coinbase posted a $667 million loss as revenue tumbled 20% Bloomberg.com [Feb 12] — the price crash is now in the volumes, and exchange earnings will lag prices on the way back up as well. Standard Chartered sees bitcoin sliding to $50,000 and ether to $1,400 before a recovery CoinDesk [Feb 12], a sell-side capitulation call that sets the downside marker.

Playbook: Stay underweight; the downside marker is Standard Chartered's $50,000 CoinDesk [Feb 12]. Prefer IBIT for any re-entry and avoid COIN and MSTR until exchange revenue stabilises. Add only if bitcoin holds above its prior completed daily close of 66,221.84 for a week (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12); cut further on a break below $50,000 CoinDesk [Feb 12].

Rates & Dollar: DXY closed at 96.93, down 2.22% over 20 sessions; TLT rose 1.33% to 89.23 and LQD 0.47% to 111.22, while HYG is down 0.31% over 20 sessions at 80.79 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). The 10Y at 4.09% and 30Y at 4.72% sit in a bull flattening over 20 observations, with the 30Y−10Y spread at +63 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-12).

Credit Check: Supply is the overhang: CNBC reports tech IPO hype is being drowned out by the prospect of $1 trillion in debt sales CNBC [Feb 12]. Investment-grade ETFs rallied with Treasuries while high yield lagged — the market is separating duration from credit risk.

Portfolio Implication: Bloomberg reports AI angst in US stocks is sending global money to Asia's winners Bloomberg.com [Feb 12]; follow it with non-US equity and keep credit in investment grade. Hold Treasuries into CPI, with TLT as the hedge for further equity weakness. Change the call if CPI is hot and yields rise while equities fall — the stock-bond correlation of an inflation scare, in which Treasuries stop hedging.

What Is Priced: The January CPI report is due out Friday morning CNBC [Feb 12]. Bonds have already leaned toward a soft outcome: the 10Y fell to 4.09% and the curve is bull flattening over 20 observations, with the 2Y at 3.47% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-12). Fed Governor Miran argues inflation is not a problem Reuters [Feb 12].

Conditional Expression: Soft core: add duration and rate-sensitive equities (homebuilders, REITs, IWM), sell VIX, buy beaten-down quality software. Hot core: the bond rally reverses — sell TLT, buy the dollar against the yen and keep defensives over growth. IWM is down 1.39% over 20 sessions at 259.54 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12), so a soft print has the most room to run there.

Risk: VIX at 20.82 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) and a likely DHS shutdown after the Senate blocked funding Reuters [Feb 12] raise the odds of a gap move either way; options are better than outright positions.

What Is Priced: Reuters reports Trump has paused China tech bans ahead of a Xi summit Reuters [Feb 12], yet markets are not pricing a thaw: KWEB fell 3.84% to 32.79 and is down 10.95% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).

Conditional Expression: Summit confirmed: buy KWEB and FXI and add US semis with China revenue. Talks stall: hedge with KWEB puts and favour domestic US chip equipment. With mainland markets closed February 16–23 investingLive [Feb 12], Hong Kong will carry the first reaction.
Risk: Congress is pushing the other way — lawmakers demand a ban on chipmaking-tool sales to China Tom's Hardware [Feb 12] — so a summit may bring trade calm without tech relief.

Catalyst & Thesis: Nvidia's next catalyst is dated Feb. 25 by a Motley Fool piece asking whether to buy before then The Motley Fool [Feb 08]. Applied Materials' post-earnings jump and its CEO's bold chip-sector call MarketWatch [Feb 12] confirm the capex pipeline feeding Nvidia's customers, and the tech-ban pause ahead of the Xi summit Reuters [Feb 12] lowers China policy risk.

Price Hurdle & Risk: NVDA closed at 186.94, down 1.64% in the prior session but up 8.76% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). The hurdle is guidance showing hyperscaler demand surviving the AI-capex debate; the risk is a guide that merely meets expectations in a tape that punishes anything short of a raise.

Catalyst & Thesis: Coinbase posted a $667 million loss with revenue down 20% Bloomberg.com [Feb 12]. Volumes follow prices, and bitcoin is down 26.01% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12), so the next quarter starts weaker still.

Price Hurdle & Risk: COIN closed at 141.09 before the results, down 7.9% on the day and 44.86% over 20 sessions from 255.86 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12). The risk to the short is crowded positioning after a near-halving; cover if the stock reclaims the pre-results close and holds it for a week.

Catalyst & Thesis: Airbnb shares rose on a revenue beat and rosy guidance CNBC [Feb 12] — in a week when the market punished every soft outlook, a raised one stands out. Travel is the discretionary category where the affluent end of the K is still spending.

Price Hurdle & Risk: No card price. The hurdle is holding the post-results gain in a risk-off tape with VIX at 20.82 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12); the risk is a hot CPI that lifts yields and compresses consumer multiples.
Observed Attention: Yahoo Finance asks whether to buy, hold or sell after Reddit stock declined 46% in a month Yahoo Finance [Feb 12] — the stock has become a retail value debate.
Motivation & Bias: Anchoring on the prior high and familiarity with the product; strong revenue growth gives holders a reason to average down.
Instrument & Risk: Use stock, not options, and wait for the shares to stop making lows. The ad-platform de-rating — Pinterest tanked on tariffs and a weak outlook CNBC [Feb 12] — is not over.

Observed Attention: After the flash crash, 24/7 Wall St. tells readers to wait and see because 'this great silver selloff is temporary' 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 12]. SLV fell 11.53% to 67.73 and is down 19.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).
Motivation & Bias: Buy-the-dip conditioning from the record run; recency bias treats a speculative top as a floor.

Instrument & Risk: Prefer GLD or gold miners to silver; if buying SLV, size small with stops. The front-month's 9.8% one-day drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12) shows how fast the leveraged layer unwinds.

Observed Attention: Memory names dominate retail screens — Yahoo Finance ran an explainer on Micron and Sandisk as the shortage fuels global RAM demand Yahoo Finance [Feb 12]; MU rose 0.88% to 413.97 on a day the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.04%, and is up 24.18% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).
Motivation & Bias: A shortage narrative plus relative strength — momentum bias toward the one AI sub-sector still rising.
Instrument & Risk: Prefer MU with defined-risk call spreads over leveraged products; Samsung's HBM4 shipments Bloomberg.com [Feb 12] are the competitive-supply risk that ends memory upcycles.

Observed Attention: Strategy is set to issue more preferred shares as its stock falls 73%, per TradingView TradingView [Feb 12]; MSTR is down 31.41% over 20 sessions at 123.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-12).
Motivation & Bias: Loyalty to the 'never sell' thesis and sunk-cost thinking; retail treats MSTR as levered upside without pricing the dilution.
Instrument & Risk: Use IBIT instead: preferred issuance dilutes common holders, and Standard Chartered's $50,000 bitcoin call CoinDesk [Feb 12] implies more downside for a leveraged proxy.
